weekThemes.title: Week 1: Get to know the muscle
weekThemes.text: You're learning to find the muscle, squeeze it and let it go completely.

weekThemes.title: Week 2: Control
weekThemes.text: Being able to contract and release whenever you want.

weekThemes.title: Week 3: Strength
weekThemes.text: Hold times and contraction strength increase.

weekThemes.title: Week 4: Recovery
weekThemes.text: A light week (days 22–30): slightly fewer contractions, same length. The muscle gets stronger by resting.

tracks.title: General Strength
tracks.text: Balanced work on holds, quick squeezes and slow squeeze–release.

tracks.title: Erection Support
tracks.text: Full-strength contractions; lying, sitting and standing in every session.
tracks.note: The home programme approach is inspired by the work of Dorey and colleagues (2004–2005). It is not a medical treatment.

tracks.title: Control and Timing
tracks.text: Coordination of quick contractions and full release, matching with the breath, awareness of relaxation.
tracks.note: The aim is to gain control and awareness; no particular result is promised.

tracks.title: Bladder Control and Dribbling
tracks.text: Slow holds, quick contractions, Knack practice and the habit of squeezing after urinating.

tracks.title: Before/After Prostate Surgery
tracks.text: A gentle start, beginning lying down and progressing to standing, plus Knack practice.
tracks.note: Unlocks only if your doctor has approved it. Don't exercise while a catheter is in place.

tracks.title: Relaxation-Focused
tracks.text: Releasing, gentle reverse Kegels and body awareness.
tracks.note: Recommended if you think your pelvic floor may be holding tension. It's a good idea to see a urologist or a pelvic floor physiotherapist.

weekThemeRestart.title: Week 1: Refresh
weekThemeRestart.text: A new month's first week: you refresh the basics and repeat the moves you've learned.

weekThemeCycle.title: Weekly cycle: keep and build
weekThemeCycle.text: After the 180 days the same 7-day cycle repeats every week: each day one move takes the lead, and day 7 is a light day. The cycle never ends; you keep and build the strength you've gained.
